ei.title: Why We Pay More for Slower but More Effortful Service
ei.subject: 6월_2023 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: Why We Pay More for Slower but More Effortful Service

fullPassage: It's hard to pay more for the speedy but highly skilled person, simply because there's less effort being observed. Two researchers once did a study in which they asked people how much they would pay for data recovery. They found that people would pay a little more for a greater quantity of rescued data, but what they were most sensitive to was the number of hours the technician worked. When the data recovery took only a few minutes, willingness to pay was low, but when it took more than a week to recover the same amount of data, people were willing to pay much more. Think about it: They were willing to pay more for the slower service with the same outcome. Fundamentally, when we value effort over outcome, we're paying for incompetence. Although it is actually irrational, we feel more rational, and more comfortable, paying for incompetence.

questions.passage: It's hard to pay more for the speedy but highly skilled person, simply because there's less effort ①<u>being observed</u>. Two researchers once did a study in which they ②<u>asked</u> people how much they would pay for data recovery. Think about it: They were willing to pay more for the slower service with the same outcome. Fundamentally, when we value effort over outcome, we're paying for incompetence. Although it is actually irrational, we feel more rational, and more comfortable, paying for incompetence.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ would paid → would pay: 조동사 would 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 would pay가 맞음
det.analysis:
❌ ① being observed — 'there's less effort being observed(관찰되는 노력이 더 적다)'. 노력이 '관찰되는' 수동 의미라 '현재분사 수동형(being + 과거분사)'을 쓴 거예요. 맞아요.

❌ ② asked — 'they asked people(사람들에게 물었다)'. 과거시제 동사라 맞아요.

✅ ③ would paid — 원문은 would pay예요. 조동사 would 뒤에는 반드시 '동사원형'이 와야 하는데, paid(과거형)를 쓰면 틀려요. 'would pay(지불할 것이다)'가 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ④ worked — 'the number of hours the technician worked(기술자가 일한 시간의 수)'. 앞 명사(hours)를 꾸미는 관계절의 과거동사라 맞아요.
det.tip: 조동사(would) + 동사원형(pay) — 과거형 paid 불가

questions.passage: It's hard ①<u>to pay</u> more for the speedy but highly skilled person, simply because there's less effort being observed. Two researchers once did a study in which they asked people how much they would pay for data recovery. They found that people would pay a little more for a greater quantity of rescued data, but what they were most sensitive to was the number of hours the technician worked. When the data recovery took only a few minutes, willingness to pay was low, but when it took more than a week ②<u>to recover</u> the same amount of data, people were willing to pay much more. Think about it: They were willing to pay more for the slower service with the same outcome. Fundamentally, when we value effort over outcome, we're paying for incompetence. ③<u>Despite</u> it is actually irrational, we feel more rational, and ④<u>more comfortable</u>, paying for incompetence.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: Despite → Although: 뒤에 '주어+동사(it is)'가 갖춰진 절이 오므로 접속사 Although가 맞음. Despite는 뒤에 명사만 오는 전치사
det.analysis:
❌ ① to pay — 'It's hard to pay more(더 내기는 어렵다)'. 가주어 It에 대응하는 진주어 to부정사라 맞아요.

❌ ② to recover — 'it took more than a week to recover(복구하는 데 일주일 넘게 걸렸다)'. 'take + 시간 + to부정사(~하는 데 시간이 걸리다)' 구조라 맞아요.

✅ ③ Despite — 원문은 Although예요. 뒤에 'it is actually irrational'처럼 주어(it)+동사(is)가 갖춰진 '절'이 오면 접속사 Although(비록 ~이지만)를 써야 해요. Despite(~에도 불구하고)는 전치사라 뒤에 명사(구)만 올 수 있어서 절 앞에는 못 와요. ←정답

❌ ④ more comfortable — 'we feel more rational, and more comfortable'. feel(느끼다) 같은 감각동사 뒤 보어 자리라 형용사가 맞고, 앞의 more rational(형용사)과 and로 나란히 이어져요.
det.tip: 뒤에 주어+동사 절 → 접속사 Although / 뒤에 명사만 → 전치사 Despite

questions.passage: It's hard to pay more for the speedy but highly skilled person, simply because there's less effort ①<u>being observed</u>. Two researchers once did a study ②<u>in which</u> they asked people how much they would pay for data recovery. They found that people would pay a little more for a greater quantity of rescued data, but ③<u>what</u> they were most sensitive to was the number of hours the technician worked. When the data recovery took only a few minutes, willingness to pay was low, but when it took more than a week to recover the same amount of data, people were willing to pay much more. Think about it: They were willing to pay more for the slower service with the same outcome. Fundamentally, when we value effort over outcome, we're paying for incompetence. Although it is actually irrational, we feel ④<u>more rationally</u>, and more comfortable, paying for incompetence.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: more rationally → more rational: feel(느끼다) 같은 감각동사의 보어 자리에는 부사가 아니라 형용사가 와야 하므로 rational이 맞음
det.analysis:
❌ ① being observed — 'there's less effort being observed(관찰되는 노력이 더 적다)'. effort는 '관찰되는(수동)' 대상이라 being+과거분사가 맞아요.

❌ ② in which — 'a study in which they asked people(사람들에게 질문한 연구)'. '전치사+관계대명사' 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오고 있어서 맞아요.

❌ ③ what — 'but what they were most sensitive to was ~'. 앞에 선행사(꾸밈 받는 명사)가 없고 '~한 것'으로 해석되는 자리라 관계대명사 what이 맞아요.

✅ ④ more rationally — 원문은 more rational이에요. feel(~하게 느끼다) 같은 감각동사 뒤 보어 자리에는 형용사를 써야 해요. 바로 뒤의 more comfortable(형용사)과 and로 나란히 이어지는 것도 힌트예요. 부사 rationally는 보어 자리에 올 수 없어 틀려요. ←정답
det.tip: feel + 형용사(보어) — 뒤의 more comfortable과 병렬인 것도 단서

questions.passage: It's hard to pay more for the speedy but highly ①<u>skilled</u> person, simply because there's less effort being observed. Two researchers once did a study in which they asked people how much they would pay for data recovery. They found that people would pay a little more for a greater quantity of rescued data, but what they were most ②<u>indifferent</u> to was the number of hours the technician worked. When the data recovery took only a few minutes, willingness to pay was low, but when it took more than a week to recover the same amount of data, people were willing to pay much more. Think about it: They were willing to pay more for the ③<u>slower</u> service with the same outcome. Fundamentally, when we value effort over outcome, we're paying for incompetence. Although it is actually ④<u>irrational</u>, we feel more rational, and more comfortable, paying for incompetence.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② indifferent → sensitive: 사람들이 일한 시간 수에 '민감하게(sensitive)' 반응했다는 내용이므로 '무관심한(indifferent)'은 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① skilled — 'the speedy but highly skilled person(빠르지만 매우 숙련된 사람)'. 뒤에서 이 사람에게 더 못 낸다는 흐름과 맞아요.

✅ ② indifferent(무관심한) — 원문은 sensitive예요. 사람들이 '가장 민감하게 반응한(most sensitive to)' 것이 기술자가 일한 시간 수라는 흐름인데, '무관심한'이라고 하면 뒤 내용(시간이 길수록 더 지불)과 정반대라 부적절해요. ←정답

❌ ③ slower — 'the slower service(더 느린 서비스)'. 같은 결과인데도 더 느린 서비스에 더 냈다는 흐름과 맞아요.

❌ ④ irrational — 'it is actually irrational(사실 비합리적이다)'. 무능에 돈을 내는 게 비합리적이라는 글의 요지와 맞아요.
det.tip: 시간에 '민감(sensitive)'하게 반응 → 무관심(indifferent)은 반대

questions.passage: It's hard to pay more for the speedy but highly skilled person, simply because there's ①<u>less effort</u> being observed. Two researchers once did a study in which they asked people how much they would pay for data recovery. They found that people would pay a little more for a greater quantity of ②<u>rescued</u> data, but what they were most sensitive to was the number of hours the technician worked. When the data recovery took only a few minutes, willingness to pay was ③<u>low</u>, but when it took more than a week to recover the same amount of data, people were willing to pay much more. Think about it: They were willing to pay more for the slower service with the same outcome. Fundamentally, when we value effort over outcome, we're paying for incompetence. Although it is actually irrational, we feel ④<u>more foolish</u>, and more comfortable, paying for incompetence.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ more foolish → more rational: 무능에 돈을 내면서도 '더 합리적이라고(more rational)' 느낀다는 역설이므로 '더 어리석게(more foolish)'는 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① less effort — 'there's less effort being observed(관찰되는 노력이 더 적다)'. 빠른 전문가에게 더 못 내는 이유로 맞아요.

❌ ② rescued — 'a greater quantity of rescued data(더 많은 양의 복구된 데이터)'. 데이터 복구 실험 맥락과 맞아요.

❌ ③ low — 'willingness to pay was low(지불 의사가 낮았다)'. 몇 분밖에 안 걸릴 때의 반응이라 맞아요.

✅ ④ more foolish(더 어리석은) — 원문은 more rational이에요. 'Although it is actually irrational(사실은 비합리적이지만)'과 대비해, 우리는 오히려 '더 합리적이고(more rational)' 편안하게 느낀다는 역설이 핵심이에요. '더 어리석게 느낀다'고 하면 뒤의 '더 편안하게 느낀다'와 안 맞아 부적절해요. ←정답
det.tip: 비합리적이지만 '더 합리적(rational)'이라 느끼는 역설 → foolish는 반대

questions.passage: It's hard to pay more for the speedy but highly skilled person, simply because there's less effort being observed. Two researchers once did a study in which they asked people how much they would pay for data recovery. They found that people would pay a little more for a greater quantity of rescued data, but what they were most sensitive to was the number of hours the technician worked. When the data recovery took only a few minutes, willingness to pay was low, but when it took more than a week to recover the same amount of data, people were willing to pay much more. Think about it: They were willing to pay more for the slower service with the same outcome. Fundamentally, when we value effort over outcome, we're paying for incompetence. Although it is __________, we feel more rational, and more comfortable, paying for incompetence.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: actually irrational — 노력에 돈을 내는 것은 '실제로는 비합리적'이지만 우리는 더 합리적이라고 느낀다는 역설
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장은 'Although it is __________, we feel more rational(그것은 __________이지만, 우리는 더 합리적이라고 느낀다)'이에요. Although(비록 ~이지만)는 앞뒤를 반대 방향으로 이어 줘요. 뒤가 '합리적으로 느낀다'니, 앞은 '실제로는 그렇지 않다'는 내용이어야 해요.

❌ ① perfectly reasonable(완전히 합리적인): 뒤의 '합리적으로 느낀다'와 같은 방향이라 Although의 대조가 깨져요.

✅ ② actually irrational(실제로는 비합리적인): 바로 앞에서 '무능(incompetence)에 돈을 내는 셈'이라고 했으니, 실제로는 비합리적이라는 결론과 정확히 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ financially smart(금전적으로 영리한): 같은 결과에 돈을 더 내는 행동이라 오히려 반대예요.

❌ ④ highly efficient(매우 효율적인): 더 느린 서비스를 고르는 것이라 효율과는 반대예요.
det.tip: Although 앞뒤는 반대 방향 — feel more rational과 대비되는 actually irrational

When the data recovery took only a few minutes, __________, but when it took more than a week to recover the same amount of data, people were willing to pay much more. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: willingness to pay was low — 복구가 몇 분 만에 끝나자 '지불 의향이 낮았다'
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장은 'When the data recovery took only a few minutes, __________, but when it took more than a week ..., people were willing to pay much more(몇 분밖에 안 걸렸을 때는 __________였지만, 일주일 넘게 걸리자 훨씬 더 내려 했다)'예요. but이 앞뒤를 반대로 이어 주고 있어요.

✅ ① willingness to pay was low(지불 의향이 낮았다): 뒤의 '훨씬 더 내려 했다'와 정반대 내용이라 but 대조에 정확히 맞아요. 글 첫 문장(노력이 덜 보이면 더 내기 어렵다)과도 이어져요. ←정답

❌ ② people happily paid much more(사람들이 기꺼이 훨씬 더 지불했다): 뒤 절과 같은 내용이 되어 but 대조가 깨져요.

❌ ③ the data was fully recovered(데이터가 완전히 복구되었다): 지불 의향을 비교하는 흐름과 관련이 없어요.

❌ ④ the technician earned more trust(기술자가 더 많은 신뢰를 얻었다): 본문에 없는 내용이에요.
det.tip: but 앞뒤 대비 — 빨리 끝나면 낮고(low), 오래 걸리면 much more

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: 'what they were most sensitive to was the number of hours the technician worked' → 가장 민감한 것은 '양'이 아니라 '일한 시간'
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문 'Two researchers once did a study in which they asked people how much they would pay for data recovery'와 일치해요.

❌ ② 본문 'When the data recovery took only a few minutes, willingness to pay was low'와 일치해요.

✅ ③ 본문은 사람들이 '기술자가 일한 시간의 수(the number of hours)'에 가장 민감했다고 했어요. 양(quantity)에는 '조금 더(a little more)'만 냈을 뿐이라, '양에 가장 민감했다'는 일치하지 않아요. ←정답(불일치)

❌ ④ 본문 'when it took more than a week ... people were willing to pay much more'와 일치해요.
det.tip: 가장 민감한 대상 = 일한 시간(hours), 양(quantity) 아님

ch: 두 연구자는 사람들이 데이터 복구에 얼마를 낼지 조사했다.
복구에 몇 분밖에 걸리지 않을 때 사람들의 지불 의사는 낮았다.
사람들은 복구된 데이터의 양에 가장 민감하게 반응했다.
복구에 일주일 넘게 걸리자 사람들은 훨씬 더 많이 지불하려 했다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: 'They were willing to pay more for the slower service with the same outcome' → 더 '느린' 서비스에 더 냈음
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문 'It's hard to pay more for the speedy but highly skilled person, simply because there's less effort being observed'와 일치해요.

✅ ② 본문은 같은 결과라면 더 '느린(slower)' 서비스에 더 냈다고 했어요. '더 빠른 서비스에 더 냈다'는 정반대라 일치하지 않아요. ←정답(불일치)

❌ ③ 본문 'They were willing to pay more for the slower service with the same outcome'과 일치해요.

❌ ④ 본문 'when we value effort over outcome, we're paying for incompetence'와 일치해요.
det.tip: 같은 결과면 더 '느린' 서비스에 더 지불 (빠른 게 아님)

ch: 숙련된 사람이 빠르게 끝내면 노력이 덜 보여 더 받기 어렵다.
사람들은 결과가 같아도 더 빠른 서비스에 기꺼이 더 많은 돈을 냈다.
결과가 같은데도 사람들은 더 느린 서비스에 더 많은 돈을 지불했다.
노력을 결과보다 중시할 때 우리는 사실상 무능에 대가를 치른다.

questions.passage: It's hard to pay more for the speedy but highly skilled person, simply because there's less effort being observed. Two researchers once did a study in which they asked people how much they would pay for data recovery. They found that people would pay a little more for a greater quantity of rescued data, but what they were most sensitive to was the number of hours the technician worked. When the data recovery took only a few minutes, willingness to pay was low, but when it took more than a week to recover the same amount of data, people were willing to pay much more. Think about it: They were willing to pay more for the slower service with the same outcome. Fundamentally, when we value effort over outcome, we're paying for incompetence. Although it is actually irrational, we feel more rational, and more comfortable, paying for incompetence.

det.korean: '~한 것' = 관계대명사 what절, '~에 민감한' = be sensitive to, '가장' = most
det.analysis:
'~하는/했던 것'은 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what으로 시작해요 → what.

'~에 민감하다'는 'be sensitive to ~'라 전치사 to로 마무리해요(민감한 대상이 what이라 to의 목적어가 앞으로 빠진 형태) → what they were most sensitive to.

det.korean: 주어 '사람들은' = people, '기꺼이 ~하려 했다' = were willing to, 동사 '지불하다' = pay, '훨씬 더 많이' = much more

'훨씬 더 많이'는 비교급을 강조하는 much more예요 → people were willing to pay much more.
